analysis:
Only the BASE text of ClusterSetupWizardLiveOperations.swift was supplied, plus a truncated patch excerpt, so I could not see the full head behavior. The visible patch adds a public `servingScope: ClusterServingScope?` setting (default nil, no behavior change on its own). It also adds a `coordinator: Bool = false` parameter to `plan(peer:keeping:coordinator:)` and touches lines near the privateGLM/MiMo probe selection (~563-565) and the assistant-quote reads (~618, 625). The patch excerpt is cut off, so I could not see how `coordinator` or `servingScope` change planning, model selection, the capability probes, or `peerMayReceive`.

The base text is unchanged context that I examined. The wizard talks to the other Mac over the paired link (ClusterSetupLinkExchange) or SSH, runs the worker and plan tool through DistributedCapabilityProbe, and hashes the worker (SHA-256) before probing. `adopt` re-decodes and rechecks the capability record before saving or sending anything. Link delivery goes into the peer's inbox, which the person must approve.

No concrete regression is visible. The default for `coordinator` is false, which preserves the previous local-only behavior.

The next pass should check the head-side use of `coordinator` and `servingScope`, in particular:
- whether a coordinator-serving plan relaxes the private image qualification gates (`privateImageQualification`, `requireCandidate`) or `peerMayReceive`;
- whether it widens what a peer can push into the inbox (see TB-011 and TB-002);
- whether it changes the authorization or attestation assumptions around serving through the coordinator (T-052, T-053, T-054).

The TB-011 and TB-002 details were oversized and not supplied, so I could not confirm those contracts.
